name: Consuelo 'Chelo' Arvizu
languages: Spanish (her first language, the Spanish of Sonora)
equipment: Buckskin coat under a heavy striped Saltillo serape, a flat-brimmed black hat tied under the chin, leather leggings
Navy revolver (Colt 1851 pattern, .36, cap-and-ball), 6 chambers loaded
Carbine (Spencer, .56 rimfire), 7 in the tube, in a saddle scabbard; bought from a discharged cavalryman in Salt Lake City
Lariat (sixty feet of braided rawhide, her own work), and a reata for the pack mules
Horse: Canela, a small, quick, cinnamon-coloured cow pony who can turn on a dollar coin
A pack train of fourteen mules with aparejos (pack saddles) and a bell mare, wintering in the corral behind Wexford's warehouse
A tally book of every load she has packed between Ninebark, Bannack and the Deer Lodge valley since June
Saddle, bedroll, a canteen, a coffee pot and a sack of pinole
features: Both Sides of the River (Borderlands origin: she speaks English and Spanish natively; among the Sonoran and Californio packers who carry most of the freight into the camps she is known to everyone, and she has advantage on Persuasion and Insight with them)

Saddle-Born (Cowhand: advantage on Riding checks; never disadvantage on ranged attacks from the saddle; mounts and dismounts with 5 ft of movement; her pony Canela gains 15 extra hit points, never spooks under her, comes to her whistle from half a mile and acts on her initiative; proficient with the lariat and throws a loop from the saddle as a bonus action)
Rawhide (Cowhand: advantage on saves against exhaustion, heat and cold; rides 12 hours a day without forced-march saves; spends one extra Hit Die on a short rest)

Cow Sense (Cowhand, 2nd level: advantage on Animal Handling with cattle, horses and mules, which in her case means mules; she turns the leaders of a stampede with one Riding or Animal Handling check, with advantage)

Outfit: Vaquero (Cowhand, 3rd level: the roping tradition of the Sonoran and Californio cattle country; her lariat reaches 40 ft, a creature she ropes from the saddle can be thrown prone and dragged without a further check, and she can rope two targets at once)

The Trail Outfit (Cattle Drover background, as a packer: any packers' camp, freighters' outfit or ranch takes her in for a night; she knows the roads, fords and passes from Salt Lake City to the Deer Lodge valley, and who on them cheats)

personality.traits: I am practical, blunt and impatient with fools, and I laugh easily at everything else. I count everything: mules, miles, dollars, men. I talk to my mules by name and I expect them to answer.
personality.ideals: A load delivered whole, on the day I said, for the price I said. That is all a packer is, and it is more than most men are.
personality.bonds: My mules, my bell mare, and my brother Ignacio, who drives the second train and is in Salt Lake City for the winter. And my contract with Obadiah Wexford, which pays for the next year.
personality.flaws: I do not trust the committee, because its men have twice told me Mexicans ought to be 'looked at', and I do not trust the road agents, because they have twice shot at my mules. I do not trust you either. I am usually right.

appearance: A compact, weathered woman of thirty-four with a broad brown face, black braids pinned under her hat, quick black eyes and a deep laugh. Dresses like a packer, because she is one: serape, leggings, spurs, a carbine on the saddle and a blacksnake whip coiled at her belt for the mules.
backstory: Consuelo Arvizu was born in 1830 near Ures in Sonora, into a family of muleteers, and was packing freight with her father across the Sonoran desert by twelve. In 1849 the family followed the gold rush to California, where Sonorans had worked the southern mines since before the Americans came and were driven out of them by a foreign miners' tax and by mobs. Her father went home. Chelo stayed, and went into packing, which is what the camps of the West run on: every sack of flour, every keg of nails and every crate of whiskey that comes over the mountains comes on a mule. She has packed to the Fraser, to Boise and, since June 1864, from Salt Lake City and Bannack to Ninebark. In late October, coming up the Bannack road by night with a late load, she saw five riders lead their horses out of the timber above the Rattlesnake Grade toward Fiddler's Station, and thought nothing of it until the robbery the next day. She has told no one, because the last time a Sonoran in a camp said she had seen something, the camp hanged a Sonoran.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Chelo is the party's guide to the roads and the freight, and their best route to the outside world: she knows every packer, every station and every pass. Play her as brisk, funny, contemptuous of nonsense, and deeply practical: she will help the party because it is good business to have the robberies stopped and because she likes people who do what they say. She is not a victim and should never be played as one; when the committee's men look at her, she looks back.
dmNotes.voice: Quick, dry, a Sonoran Spanish accent, switching to Spanish when she is annoyed or fond. Calls the party by surnames until she likes them. Swears at mules with real artistry.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: get her mules and her contract through the winter. Secondary: stop the road agents, who shoot at mules. Tertiary: see that what was done to Patrick Kehoe, whom she liked, is not done to anyone else, including herself.
dmNotes.secrets: CLUE D3: on the night of Wednesday 19 October, coming up the Bannack road after dark, she saw five riders lead their horses out of the timber above the Rattlesnake Grade and up the slope toward Fiddler's Station, and the station's barn door open to let them in. The next morning the Thursday coach was robbed on the grade. She will tell the party if they earn her trust and promise that it will not be her word alone against a white man's (vg-scenario-002). She also knows Deadfall Canyon: she wintered mules there in 1863, and she knows there is a cabin in it and a way in from the top that nobody uses (vg-scenario-004).
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: businesslike, testing; warm once trust is earned. Toward Benicio Aranda, if he is played: an old acquaintance from the Boise road, teasing and fond. Toward Gabriel Tennant: a friend, her mules' farrier. Toward Wexford: her employer, whom she thinks is a fool but not a bad one. Toward Sefton: neutral; he buys her flour.
